extracted.intended_audience: researchers and research administrators applying to Royal Society funding (UK and international)
extracted.subtask_description: High-level guidance and principles governing Royal Society grant and fellowship schemes, intended to guide applicants and host institutions about priorities, values, and procedural touchpoints (dates, application process, training).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Our work is guided by the principles of Excellence; Inclusivity; Flexibility; and Openness and Fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four named principles are the stated frame for the Royal Society's funding decisions and processes; applicants should expect their proposals and behaviour as award-holders to be judged against these values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for discovery-led and applied research
rubrics_metrics.description: We support scientists pursuing discovery-led and applied research through a wide range of schemes and career development opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding is available for both basic (discovery-led) and applied research projects; applicants should position proposals within these research aims where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of diversity and inclusive applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Society recognises that diversity is essential for delivering excellence in STEM, and wants to encourage applications from the widest range of backgrounds, perspectives and experiences to maximise innovation and creativity in science for the benefit of humanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and host institutions should consider and, where relevant, evidence diversity/inclusivity practices; the Society explicitly values widening applicant diversity as part of its assessment ethos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for outstanding researchers / excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships and grants for outstanding researchers — We support scientists pursuing discovery-led and applied research through a wide range of schemes and career development opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schemes are targeted at outstanding researchers; competitiveness and excellence of the candidate and proposal are focal expectations across the portfolio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of specific scheme — Royal Society Wolfson Fellowship
rubrics_metrics.description: The five-year Royal Society Wolfson Fellowships enables UK universities and not-for-profit research institutions to attract and recruit talented…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indicates scheme-specific aims (attracting/recruiting talented researchers) and a defined award duration; applicants should align applications to the stated recruitment/host-institution objective and eligibility (UK universities and not-for-profit research institutions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of freedom, support and flexibility to researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Society funding provides freedom, support and flexibility to researchers in the UK and internationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can expect funded projects to be supported in ways that prioritise researcher autonomy and flexible use of funds within scheme rules; proposals should describe how the funding will enable independent research and career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to application process and key dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The application process — A step-by-step guide to the application and assessment process for our schemes. Application dates — See key dates for funding schemes, with open, close and decision dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow the published application and assessment process and meet published opening, closing and decision deadlines; procedural compliance (timely submission, correct forms) is implied as required for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations around training and development for award-holders
rubrics_metrics.description: Training and development — Find out about the tailored career development and engagement opportunities available to many of our grant-holders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award-holders are expected to engage with Royal Society-provided career development and engagement opportunities; applicants should be prepared to participate in such activities if funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Society policies and positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and positions — View the policies and positions underpinning our grants portfolio – relevant to all applicants and award holders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and award-holders must comply with the Royal Society's policies (ethical, eligibility, data, host institution requirements, etc.); proposals should be consistent with those policies and be prepared to adhere to them if funded.
